For each asset-day, the day-ahead battery arbitrage spread ranks hourly day-ahead energy price and credits the highest battery_duration hours as discharge revenue and debits the lowest battery_duration hours as charging cost, leaving all other hours at zero. The resulting per-day net spread is converted from $/MWh to $/kWh (÷1000) and scaled by year_hours to express the value in $/kW-yr

For each asset-day, the real-time battery arbitrage spread ranks hourly real-time energy price and credits the highest battery_duration hours as discharge revenue and debits the lowest battery_duration hours as charging cost, leaving all other hours at zero. The resulting per-day net spread is converted from $/MWh to $/kWh (÷1000) and scaled by year_hours to express the value in $/kW-yr

AC-deliverable solar natural capacity factor: DC power (solar_natural_capacity_factor_dc * nominal_capacity_mw_dc) clipped at the AC nameplate (the inverter limit) and normalized by the AC nameplate. Realizes ILR economics -- oversizing lifts low-irradiance shoulders while the clip shaves clear-sky peaks to AC nameplate. Equals least(1, solar_natural_capacity_factor_dc * ILR). Distinct from solar_natural_capacity_factor_dc, which is the pre-inverter DC signal and may exceed 1.0.

Pre-inverter DC capacity factor: temperature-derated ratio of plane-of-array irradiance to STC (1000 W/m2), against the DC array rating. May exceed 1.0 at clear-sky peaks (POA > 1000 W/m2). Raw DC signal before inverter clipping; the AC-deliverable value is solar_natural_capacity_factor.

Plane-of-array irradiance on the generalized collector (W/m2) via Erbs decomposition + Hay-Davies transposition, parameterized by solar_type through solar_system_tilt_angle / solar_system_azimuth_angle. POA = DNI*cos(AOI) + DHI*[Ai*Rb + (1-Ai)*(1+cos tilt)/2] + GHI*albedo*(1-cos tilt)/2. Mirrors the plane_irradiance_* engine; flat config returns GHI exactly.

The effective azimuth of the solar collection plane at a given timestamp, by configuration. Flat and fixed-tilt hold the configured collector azimuth (180, south). Single-axis tracking flips between axis_azimuth+90 and axis_azimuth-90 (east-facing before solar noon, west-facing after) based on the sign of the horizontal-axis rotation angle -- it does NOT continuously track solar azimuth like a vertical-axis tracker would. Dual-axis tracks solar azimuth dynamically.

The effective tilt of the solar collection plane from horizontal at a given timestamp, by configuration. Flat is 0; fixed-tilt holds a static tilt equal to latitude. Single-axis tracking derives tilt from the horizontal N-S-axis rotation angle (Braun & Mitchell 1983 formula, matches pvlib.tracking.singleaxis with axis_azimuth = solar_collector_azimuth, max_angle = 90) -- tilt sweeps from near-90 deg at sunrise/sunset down to 0 at solar noon. Dual-axis varies continuously with solar zenith.

Aggressive mitigation scenario in which total greenhouse gas emissions reduce to net zero by 2050. Warming outcome: Global average temperatures rise 1.3–2.4°C by 2100, consistent with the goals of the Paris Agreement. Underlying SSP narrative: SSP1 ('Sustainability / Taking the Green Road') — global society shifts toward sustainable development, reduced inequality, and lower resource/energy intensity.

Strong mitigation scenario in which total greenhouse gas emissions stabilize at current levels until 2050 and then decline through 2100. Warming outcome: Global average temperatures rise 2.1–3.5°C by 2100. Underlying SSP narrative: SSP2 ('Middle of the Road') — social, economic, and technological trends continue without marked departure from historical patterns; uneven development progress across countries.

Limited mitigation scenario in which total greenhouse gas emissions double by 2100. Warming outcome: Global average temperatures rise 2.8–4.6°C by 2100. Underlying SSP narrative: SSP3 ('Regional Rivalry / A Rocky Road') — resurgent nationalism, regional conflicts, weak international cooperation, declining investment in education/technology.

Low mitigation scenario in which total greenhouse gas emissions triple by 2075. Warming outcome: Global average temperatures rise 3.3–5.7°C by 2100. Underlying SSP narrative: SSP5 ('Fossil-Fueled Development / Taking the Highway') — rapid, fossil-fuel-intensive economic growth with high energy demand and faith in technological solutions over environmental constraints.
